newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN WANT PEACE AND THE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN WANT PEACE AND THE TITLE.

text.p: Even more success and less fuss is what coach Giovanni Trapattoni is hoping for as Bayern Munich enter a new season in which they will go for yet another German title.
"I think the players understood from last season that squabbling does not bring you anywhere," said Trapattoni, who led Bayern to a record 14th crown after a campaign marred by controversy.
The Italian made it clear that he would not be happy with just the title and that he expected to see his stars shine on the European scene as well.
"The title is our priority but we also have the talent to reach the European Cup final," said Trapattoni, whose side looks just as strong as last year's, if not stronger.
Bayern, who will be at home to Kaiserslautern in their first league match on Saturday, warmed up for their Bundesliga campaign by winning the new League Cup pre-season tournament.
They knocked out rivals Borussia Dortmund in the semifinals before beating VfB Stuttgart 2-0 in the final on Saturday.
Several influential players, such as striker Juergen Klinsmann and defender Christian Ziege, now with Sampdoria and AC Milan respectively, have left.

But Bayern have bought strong players to replace them. The most spectacular signing was Brazilian striker Giovane Elber, who joined from Stuttgart for a 12.5-million-dollar ($6.9-million) transfer fee.
Another newcomer is French international defender Bixente Lizarazu, who signed from Athletic Bilbao and should take up a new role as a midfielder.
"We've lost good players but we've gained good ones, who are fitting in nicely," said Trapattoni.
Germany's richest club earned the nickname FC Hollywood last season after having to cast aside an array of scandals.

Klinsmann, who was embroiled in a public row with club captain Lothar Matthaeus and once yelled at Trapattoni after being substituted, said he was leaving because he was fed up with the atmosphere at the club.
Chairman Franz Beckenbauer has often been very critical of a team of highly-paid internationals who had to hold crisis meetings when results did not go their way.
Trapattoni, who needed a symbol in his search for a more relaxed atmosphere, replaced Matthaeus as team captain with the quieter Thomas Helmer.
According to Elber, Bayern is not as bad as it seems.
"Lots of people had warned me by telling me all sorts of nasty things about Bayern but there were not true," he said. "I found a bunch of really nice guys."
But Elber did notice some differences. "Everything is bigger here," he said. "Some 500 people watch us every time we train. In Stuttgart, we had about 50."
Asked about his new role, the gifted Brazilian, who scored 17 goals for Stuttgart last season, said he would be happy to work for others.
"Scoring goals is not the only thing in football," he said. "If I score 10 goals and if we're champions, I'll be happy."
